title: Sell Mineral Rights in Peterman, AL
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Peterman, AL | Monroe County
metaDescription: Own mineral rights near Peterman, AL in rural Monroe County? Get a straightforward, courthouse-checked offer, no pressure to sign anything.
heroLead: Peterman is a small rural community in Monroe County where mineral ownership tends to run through a handful of long-established farming families rather than any corporate or industrial history.
intro: In a community this size, the story behind most mineral interests is simple to state even if the title work to confirm it takes some effort: land farmed by the same family for generations, occasionally approached by a landman during one of south Alabama's periodic exploratory leasing rounds, and rarely revisited since. Whether that old lease is still active, expired, or was never signed at all is usually the first thing worth sorting out before talking about value.

sections.heading: Farming Families, Occasional Leasing Interest
paragraphs: If your family has farmed near Peterman for generations, the mineral question usually comes down to whether a lease was ever signed and, if so, whether it's still active today. We check the Monroe County record directly rather than relying on family memory of an old conversation with a landman decades ago.

sections.heading: What We Check Before Naming a Number
paragraphs: We confirm your family's exact ownership at the courthouse, check whether the tract has ever been leased or drilled, and look at any nearby activity in Monroe County that might inform value for an untested parcel. That combination gives us an honest starting point, whether your interest turns out to be producing, leased-but-undrilled, or entirely untested.

faqs.question: A landman approached our family decades ago but we're not sure what happened after that. How do we find out?
faqs.answer: We check the Monroe County record for any recorded lease on your tract and confirm whether it's still active, expired, or was never finalized.

faqs.question: Our farm has never had a well on it. Is there any reason to talk to you?
faqs.answer: Yes — we look at your tract against nearby activity in the county and give you an honest read on speculative value, even without a production history.

faqs.question: How do we know exactly what our family owns after several generations of farming the same land?
faqs.answer: We trace the deed and probate history at the Monroeville courthouse to confirm current ownership before we discuss anything else.

faqs.question: Does it matter that Peterman is a very small community?
faqs.answer: No, we research the courthouse record the same way regardless of how small the community is. What matters is your specific tract's history.

faqs.question: How long does the whole process usually take from first contact to closing?
faqs.answer: For a straightforward, single-family interest, it's often a few weeks from the time we confirm title to closing.
